requirements.title: Departmental/Program Major Course Requirements (51–53 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete Areas A–E. Major courses cannot double count within the major; the calculus route determines the published credit range.

requirements.title: Area C: Additional Philosophy Course Requirements (9 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete 3 credits in each of the three listed subject areas.

requirements.title: Area A: Required Courses (16 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete the listed courses.

requirements.title: Area B: Required Computer Science Courses (20-22 credits)
requirements.summary: Five fixed CS courses plus one calculus route; published total 20–22 credits.

requirements.title: Calculus alternatives
requirements.summary: MA 16010 AND MA 16020, OR MA 16100, OR MA 16500. These are three routes, not four fixed math courses.

requirements.title: Ethics/ Value Theory (3 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete the stated credit load from this pool.

requirements.title: History of Philosophy (3 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete the stated credit load from this pool.

requirements.title: Philosophy of Science, Tech, and Mathematics (3 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete the stated credit load from this pool.

requirements.title: Area D: Breadth Requirement (3 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete the stated credit load from this pool.

requirements.title: Area E: Research Requirement (3 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete 3 credits of PHIL 41500; the course itself permits 1–3 credits per enrollment.

requirements.title: Note for Areas C & D
requirements.summary: At least 6 credits across Areas C and D must be at the 30000+ level. The later course note specifies the 30000–50000 level; retain both source formulations.

requirements.title: Other Departmental - Liberal Arts Core (35-76 credits)
requirements.summary: Published CLA core range: 35–76 credits. Complete the applicable diversity and foundational requirements; overlap is allowed outside the major. Degree + students with a second major outside CLA are exempt from the CLA core.

requirements.title: Core I: Disciplinary Diversity (6-18 credits)
requirements.summary: Take one course in each of six different CLA disciplines, distinguished by prefix; undistributed credit does not satisfy this rule. Published range: 6–18 credits. Accreditation-based exemptions are conditional.

requirements.title: Core II: Social Diversity (1-3 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete one course from the linked Social Diversity Selective List; published range: 1–3 credits. The approved list is not yet extracted here.

requirements.title: Core III: Linguistic Diversity (8-16 credits)
requirements.summary: Complete 10100, 10200, 20100 and 20200 OR 10500 and 20500 in one world language; published range: 8–16 credits. Exact eligible language/proficiency details require advising; no generic codes are invented.

requirements.title: Foundational Requirements (21-36 credits)
requirements.summary: Meet AI working competency, humanities, behavioral/social science, information literacy, two science requirements, science/technology/society, written communication, oral communication and quantitative reasoning with approved coursework. Published range: 21–36 credits; courses can overlap CLA diversity requirements. The approved university pools are not extracted for this BA.

requirements.title: Notes
requirements.summary: Double counting is allowed across the plan except within major requirements. Programs whose accreditation is threatened by CLA Core I/II can be exempt from those categories but still require Core III. Degree + students with a second major outside CLA are exempt from the CLA core; applicability is conditional.

requirements.title: Electives (0-34 credits)
requirements.summary: Published general elective range: 0–34 credits. This is not an additional fixed load or a named required course pool.

requirements.title: GPA Requirements
requirements.summary: Maintain a 2.0 GPA in courses applying toward the PHIL major, with no P/NP fulfillment, and a 2.0 graduation GPA for the BA.

requirements.title: Course Requirements and Notes
requirements.summary: PHIL 15000 cannot count toward the major. Courses used for Areas A, B or C cannot count for Area D. At least 6 credits in Areas C and D must be at the 30000–50000 level.

requirements.title: College of Liberal Arts Pass/No Pass Option Policy
requirements.summary: P/NP cannot fulfill CLA core, major, minor or certificate requirements.

requirements.title: University Core Requirements
requirements.summary: Meet all ten listed university foundational outcomes, including AI working competency and two science requirements. The Senate maintains approved selectives; these obligations overlap the CLA foundational list and are not counted twice.

requirements.title: Civics Literacy Proficiency Requirement
requirements.summary: The catalog directs all baccalaureate students to complete 12 Civics Literacy podcasts and episode quizzes, then the knowledge test. The requirement bears no financial costs and does not affect GPA; do not invent a credit-bearing course.

requirements.title: Upper Level Requirement
requirements.summary: Complete resident study at Purdue for at least two semesters and at least 32 approved semester hours required for the degree, expected to be junior level (30000+) or above. These may overlap major coursework.

requirements.title: Pre-Requisite Information
requirements.summary: The catalog directs prerequisite checks to authenticated myPurdue. Current prerequisites remain unverified; missing values do not mean no prerequisites.

requirements.title: World Language Courses
requirements.summary: The catalog lists offered languages but states that acceptable languages and required proficiency vary by program and require advising. No language offering is inferred to be a fixed BA course.

notes: The 2026–2027 catalog governs this mapped curriculum. The department overview, modified October 15, 2025, still reports eight philosophy courses/24 hours and an older five-CS list totaling 15 hours. Those figures and CS 10100 membership conflict with the current catalog and are retained as historical source context, not merged into its requirements.

Six philosophy identities are fixed (five in Area A plus PHIL 41500 in Area E); three additional philosophy selections are required in Area C. The four math listings form three alternative routes, including a two-course bundle, rather than four fixed math courses.
No concentration or track is defined in the reviewed BA catalog; Areas A–E are required curricular sections, not separate awards. The Purdue BS and ECE concentration remain separate programs.

The catalog was read in the authorized laptop Chrome browser and saved for local parser verification on October 12, 2026. Supported web fetch returned HTTP 403; no restriction bypass or authenticated prerequisite access was attempted.

The mapped major inventory is complete within Areas A–E. The whole degree remains partial because the linked social-diversity and university approved pools and advisor-specific language eligibility are not fully extracted. No full independent second-pass certification is claimed.

outcomes.text: Examine privacy, bias and responsible technology alongside programming and data skills.
Career examples include policy analysis, user experience design and project management; these are prospective paths, not placement statistics.
Identify central AI concepts and algorithms.
Explain principles of machine learning, neural networks and other AI techniques.
Summarize AI ethics and societal impacts.
Evaluate strengths and limitations of AI approaches.
Develop reasoned critiques of AI research papers and projects.

overview: A 120-credit BA offered through Philosophy in the College of Liberal Arts at West Lafayette. The 2026–2027 catalog combines philosophical analysis of AI, programming and AI methods, a choice of calculus routes, further philosophy selections, interdisciplinary breadth and a research practicum. The major requires 51–53 credits; broader CLA and university requirements also apply.
